about: MUTATING — retire ONE PersistentVolumeClaim, and through a Delete reclaim its Longhorn volume and bytes (infra/forge/retire-volume-claim.sh <namespace> <claim> <plan_sha256>; backlog f36eb7ce, design b4b1c99d). Decided by David 2026-10-18 on f36eb7ce's design review: a claim is never retired by hand from a workstation — 'manually running any ops command is a gap in BOSS coverage' — so this verb replaces the admin-kubeconfig step delete-orphan-object deliberately left a named human one, and that kind floor is unchanged. AUTHORISED PER RUN BY DAVID'S PASSKEY, design 17835005: the read-only plan-a-volume-claim-retirement renders bytes onto the approve step, an allowed passkey signs them, and the runner hands this write sha256 of the SIGNED plan. THE AUTHORITY IS DERIVED, as delete-orphan-object's is: the script re-renders at call time and acts only when the plan still hashes to the approved value — the name is not protected (pgdata-postgres-0, boss-dev-work, in any namespace); the manifest directories are clean in git; undeclared-objects.sh --check names the claim undeclared (refusing an unowned namespace, a declared claim, an exempt or controller-owned one, and one not live); the claim is not being deleted and has no owner; its volume names it by uid and reclaims by Retain or by Delete on a detached Longhorn volume; and nothing in its namespace mounts it or would stamp it again. Any drift refuses (exit 78) naming both hashes, and a second run of an applied plan finds the claim gone and refuses, so one approval deletes at most once. One claim per request. CAPTURE BEFORE DELETE, ON THE RECORD: the PVC, PV and Longhorn volume YAML are attached to this ops-request through boss attach, which reads the bytes back; only a verified attachment lets the delete run, and the capture is printed on stdout too. THE WRITE is one DELETE carrying DeleteOptions.preconditions.uid, so a same-named claim recreated in the race is refused by the API server. THE EFFECT: the claim read back gone (NotFound, or its name held by another uid); for Delete, the PV and the Longhorn volume read back NotFound within the wait; for Retain, the PV read back kept. Only that complete read-back prints the effect line; a claim held Terminating, a volume that outlives its Delete reclaim, or an unreadable answer exits 1 naming what it saw. Initial refusals exit 78 without writes. Timeout 600 covers the derivation's parse, the attach, and three 180 s read-backs.
effect: ^retire-volume-claim: PersistentVolumeClaim [a-z0-9-]+/[a-z0-9.-]+ uid [0-9a-f-]{36} is gone \(read back: [^)]+\); (PersistentVolume [^ ]+ \(reclaim policy Delete\) is gone \(read back: [^)]+\); Longhorn volume [^ ]+ is gone \(read back: [^)]+\)|PersistentVolume [^ ]+ \(reclaim policy Retain\) is kept, phase [A-Za-z]+ — its bytes stand; this verb deletes no PersistentVolume|it was bound to no PersistentVolume)$
